speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help you, please describe exactly what you feel when the room seems to spin, and how long this episode has lasted. Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea alongside this symptom?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief duration of the episode (3 minutes) and lack of associated hearing loss strongly point to BPPV rather than Meniere's disease or a central cause.
